why: This is Meeting Rooms II with names attached: rentals are half-open intervals, and the minimum number of cars equals the maximum overlap. Sweep rentals by pickup time, keep busy cars in a min-heap by return time, and reuse the lowest-numbered free car.
hints: A car is just a 'room' that holds non-overlapping intervals. How many cars do you need at the busiest moment?
Sort by pickup time. Before assigning a rental, release every car whose return time is <= this pickup (half-open intervals). Reuse a free car if there is one, otherwise open a new car.
Two heaps: busy (returnTime, carId) and free carIds, so the smallest free id is reused. O(n log n). Then print each car's record ids in the order assigned.
pitfalls: Endpoints touch: a car returned at time 3 can take a pickup at time 3 (use <=, not <).
The input is unsorted; sort by pickup time (then return time, then record id).
A zero-length rental [t, t) goes to car 0 and does not make car 0 busy; create car 0 if it does not exist yet.
Always reuse the lowest-numbered free car, or the output ids will differ.
statement:
You are given an unsorted list of rental records. Each record is [recordId, pickupTime, returnTime]; recordId is unique.

Assign every rental to a car so that no car has two overlapping rentals, using the minimum number of cars. Rentals are half-open intervals [pickupTime, returnTime), so a car returned at time t can be picked up again at time t.

Assignment rules (so the answer is unique):

  • Process rentals in order of pickup time (ties: earlier return time, then smaller recordId).
  • Give a rental the free car with the smallest id; if no car is free, create a new car whose id is the next integer (0, 1, 2, ...).
  • A zero-duration rental [t, t) goes to car 0 (creating car 0 if needed) and does not make car 0 busy.

Return one string per car, in car-id order, of the form "carId: recordId recordId ...", listing that car's records in the order they were assigned.

Example: [[101,1,3],[102,2,4],[103,4,6]]

  • 101 (time 1 to 3): no car is free, create car 0.
  • 102 (time 2 to 4): car 0 is busy until 3, create car 1.
  • 103 (time 4 to 6): car 0 was returned at 3 and car 1 at 4, both free; pick the smaller id, car 0.

Result: ["0: 101 103", "1: 102"].
